docs.title: Deploy sources
docs.text: A deploy happened and the radar did not judge it: follow the event from the sender to the engine and find where it stopped.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The radar judges a deploy only after it has been told about it. The event travels in four steps, and it can stop at any of them. Each step leaves a trace, so the question "where did it stop" has an answer.

flowchart LR
  S["Sender<br/>Argo, Flux, CI"]:::ext
  R["Webhook route<br/>DeploySource"]:::radar
  K["Deployment or StatefulSet<br/>finishes a rollout"]:::k8s
  W["Native watch<br/>sourceType: kubernetes"]:::radar
  ST["Event store<br/>PostgresWatch"]:::radar
  E["Attribution engine<br/>deploy registered"]:::out
  S -->|"2: request reaches the manager"| R
  R -->|"3: event stored"| ST
  K --> W
  W -->|"synthesised"| ST
  ST -->|"4: registered"| E

The numbers are the steps of the checklist below; step 1 is the DeploySource being ready. A native source replaces the sender and the route with the manager watching the workload itself.

docs.title: A deploy never shows up
docs.text: Work down this list. Stop at the first step that fails.

docs.title: 1. Is the DeploySource ready?
docs.text:
kubectl get pgds -n <ns>
kubectl describe pgds <name> -n <ns>
Phase Path What it means Go to Ready /webhook/<ns>/<name> the route is live step 2 Ready empty, source type kubernetes watched natively, no route by design Native watch Pending empty the PostgresWatch it points to does not exist or is not running PostgresWatchNotReady Failed empty the spec is invalid InvalidSpec

docs.title: 2. Did the request reach the manager?
docs.text:
Send a test event by hand and read the answer. Only the leader listens on the webhook port, so go to the leader and not to a Service that may pick a standby:

LEADER=$(kubectl get lease -n <ns> pg-regression-radar-manager.radar.pgregressionradar.io \
  -o jsonpath='{.spec.holderIdentity}' | cut -d_ -f1)
kubectl -n <ns> port-forward pod/$LEADER 8080:8080 &
curl -i -X POST localhost:8080/webhook/<ns>/<name> \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"app":"<app>","namespace":"<ns>","revision":"test-1","timestamp":"2026-11-27T12:00:00Z"}'

Use a throwaway revision: the test is a real event and will be judged like any other. The status says where it stopped:

Answer Meaning Fix 204 No Content accepted, or accepted and dropped: see step 3 401 Unauthorized the DeploySource has a webhookSecret and the request has no, or a wrong, X-Webhook-Token send the header; see Webhook authentication 400 Bad Request the body is not the format of the source type compare with Deploy sources 404 Not Found no route at that path: wrong namespace or name, or the source is not Ready kubectl get pgds and use its Path 503 Service Unavailable with Retry-After: 10 the PostgresWatch behind the source is not running (restarting or being deleted) wait; senders that retry deliver the event once it is back 500 from an otlp source its span mapping is unusable the log says why: ingester: otlp source is misconfigured connection refused nothing listens: you reached a standby, or the port is wrong use the leader; check --webhook-bind-address

A Service can send an event to a standby

The webhook, the metrics and the verdict listeners run on the leader only. A Service that selects every manager pod sends a share of requests to standbys, which refuse the connection. Senders that retry get through on a later try; one that does not is lost. If events disappear only some of the time, this is the first thing to check: send the same request a few times through the Service and count the refusals.

docs.title: 3. Was it stored?
docs.text:
kubectl logs -n <ns> -l app.kubernetes.io/component=manager --since=1h | grep 'deploy event'
  • ingester: deploy event stored (with id, app, revision): it arrived and was kept. Continue to step 4.
  • ingester: deploy event ignored, its app is not the one this source is configured for (debug level; run with --log-level=debug): the event's app is not the DeploySource's spec.appName. The sender still got 204. Fix appName, or the app the sender reports.
  • ingester: rejected webhook request with invalid or missing token: step 2, 401.
  • ingester: deploy event not stored, the watch this source feeds is not running: step 2, 503.
  • No line at all: the request did not reach this manager. Check the sender: its URL, its retries and its own delivery log.

docs.title: 4. Was it registered with the engine?
docs.text:
When the PostgresWatch has attribution.enabled, a stored event is followed by:

attribution: deploy registered, it will be judged from 10 to 45 minutes after it

with firstEvaluation and lastEvaluation bounding when the verdict arrives. See DeployRegistered. Nothing before the first evaluation is a decision, so a deploy that is five minutes old has no verdict yet.

docs.title: 5. Why does the engine not act on it?
docs.text: That is a different problem: see Enforce mode.

docs.title: A native source reports nothing
docs.text:
A kubernetes source reports a deploy when the Deployment or StatefulSet named by appName finishes rolling out to a new revision, the same signal as kubectl rollout status. A half-finished rollout is never reported. Check:

  • appName is the name of the workload itself, and the workload is in the same namespace as the DeploySource.
  • workloadKind is right (Deployment or StatefulSet).
  • The rollout completed. kubectl rollout status deploy/<name> -n <ns>.
  • The manager may read Deployments and StatefulSets. Its default ClusterRole does; a custom one may not.
  • Look for workloadwatch: deploy event synthesised from native rollout in the log. Seeing it means the radar got the deploy; the next place to look is step 4. If the watch was not ready at that moment you see workloadwatch: postgresWatchRef not ready yet, and the event is retried: PostgresWatchNotReady.

docs.title: An Argo Rollouts deploy is judged but never paused
docs.text: Pausing and aborting only apply to a deploy that an argo-rollouts DeploySource reported, because the radar needs the Rollout to patch. A deploy from generic, argocd, flux, otlp or a native source is judged and logged but never acted on; the log says NotArgoRollout. See Enforce mode.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Deploy sources and webhooks: every source type, its payload and its authentication.
  • Reason codes
  • Where to look

docs.title: Nothing is detected
docs.text: The radar runs without errors and never reports a regression: how to tell "nothing regressed" from "it cannot see".

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Silence has two very different causes. Either nothing got slower, or the radar is not in a position to tell. Check in this order: is it reading the database, does it hold enough history, and is the deploy the radar judges one it knows about.

docs.title: 1. Is it reading the database?
docs.text:
kubectl get pgw <name> -n <ns>
kubectl get pgw <name> -n <ns> -o json | jq '.status | {phase, trackedQueryIds, lastScrapeTime, conditions: [.conditions[] | {type, status, reason}]}'
You see It means Go to Phase: Failed the watch's worker never started DSNUnresolved, SecretsUnresolved, WorkerStartFailed Collecting is False with NoScrapeYet no scrape has completed since the worker started NoScrapeYet Collecting is False with ScrapeStale scrapes stopped or are failing ScrapeStale Collecting is True and Tracked Queries is 0 it connects but sees no statements Setup and the database (extension, permissions) Collecting is True and queries are tracked it is reading; continue below

The same facts are metrics: pg_regression_radar_collector_scrapes_total should rise once per interval, ..._collector_scrape_errors_total should not, and ..._collector_tracked_queries should be above zero. See Metrics.

For the one-binary operator there are no conditions; read its log for collector: scrape failed and run it with --dry-run.

docs.title: 2. Does it have enough to compare?
docs.text:
If the radar runs without errors but never reports a regression, check these in order:

  1. The counters were reset. After pg_stat_statements_reset() or a server restart, the radar logs collector: pg_stat_statements counters restarted for query; using activity since the reset. It then needs new samples before it can compare windows.
  2. Not enough data yet. A window needs minSamples scrape intervals with activity and minExecutions calls. See Detection algorithm.
  3. The query is outside the top 500. Each scrape reads the 500 busiest statements.
  4. Its own queries are excluded. Statements containing pg_stat_statements are filtered out on purpose.

In Kubernetes, PerformanceRegression objects report Detected, NoRegression or InsufficientData; the last one means case 2.

To see why a query was not reported, run the manager at --log-level=debug for one deploy and read the correlation: lines for its query: correlation: insufficient data, correlation: no change point found, correlation: t-test result (with the p_value) and correlation: detection did not survive multiple-testing each say which test stopped it. See the log catalog.

docs.title: 3. Does it know about the deploy?
docs.text:
A deploy-triggered check needs a deploy event. If regressions are found only by the periodic check, or never, the deploy may not be reaching the radar: see A deploy never shows up.

A deploy that arrives before the radar holds enough history is not lost: it is retried until its analysis window closes. pg_regression_radar_pending_deploy_events counts them, and correlation: deploy event registered for retry and correlation: deploy event's analysis window elapsed bracket the wait.

docs.title: 4. It detected something and nothing arrived
docs.text: A regression that passed every test is written as a PerformanceRegression, counted in pg_regression_radar_regressions_detected_total, and sent to the alert destination. If the object exists and the message did not arrive, see Alerts and the dashboard.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Where to look
  • Detection algorithm and Collector internals

docs.title: Enforce mode
docs.text: Why the engine judged a deploy and did not pause or abort it, what to check before you let it act, and how to stop and restart it.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The attribution engine works in steps, and each one is a place it can stop. Knowing which step a deploy reached is most of the diagnosis.

flowchart LR
  D["Deploy registered"]:::radar
  J["Judged<br/>10 to 45 min after,<br/>every 5 min"]:::radar
  X{"Decision"}:::gate
  L["none or alert:<br/>logged, never acts"]:::gate
  V["hold or rollback:<br/>verdict served<br/>(enforce mode)"]:::radar
  C["Rollout controller<br/>polls the verdict"]:::ext
  M["Manager pauses<br/>or aborts the Rollout"]:::out
  K["Abort checked<br/>15 min later"]:::gate
  D --> J --> X
  X -->|"none, alert"| L
  X -->|"hold, rollback"| V
  V -->|"actuate off"| C
  V -->|"actuate on"| M
  M -->|"abort"| K

Each box is a place a deploy can stop. In shadow mode the path ends at the decision: the verdict is always pass and the decision is only logged.

  • Shadow mode (attribution.mode: shadow, the default) judges and logs. The verdict is always pass, and nothing is written to a Rollout.
  • Enforce serves a verdict for a rollout controller to poll, and a decision is acted on only if the controller asks.
  • Enforce with actuate.enabled lets the manager itself pause (hold) or abort (rollback) the Rollout.

A deploy cannot be convicted before about 15 minutes after it. Everything below assumes the Rollout waits that long.

docs.title: Read the three conditions first
docs.text:
The status of the watch already says which step is blocked. Actuating is the one that answers "may it act right now".

kubectl get pgw <name> -n <ns> -o json | jq '.status.conditions[] | select(.type=="Actuating" or .type=="ArmsLog" or .type=="Collecting") | {type, status, reason, message}'

Actuating has a single reason at a time, and they are checked in this order:

Actuating is Reason What it means Fix False BreakerOpen earlier aborts did not help, so the engine only alerts close the breaker after finding out why False ShadowMode the watch is in shadow mode set attribution.mode: enforce once the shadow decisions look right False ActuationNotAsked enforce, without attribution.actuate.enabled enable actuate, or let the rollout controller act on the verdict False NoActuator actuate is on and the manager cannot patch Rollouts set manager.autoAbort.rbacEnabled: true in the chart False ActuationPaused the kill switch annotation is set remove it True ActuationReady the manager may pause and abort Rollouts nothing: if a deploy was not acted on, see below

docs.title: Before you turn enforce on
docs.text:
Run this once, in order. Each line is a way a first real regression has gone unhandled.

  1. Run shadow mode first, and compare. Leave the watch in shadow for a few deploys. For each, compare the decision line's action with what happened. The verdict endpoint's wouldBe shows what enforce would have said. Turn enforce on when you would have agreed with the engine.

    kubectl logs -n <ns> -l app.kubernetes.io/component=manager --since=24h \
  | jq -r 'select(.msg | startswith("attribution (shadow)")) | "\(.time) \(.deploy) \(.action) grade=\(.grade) \(.reasons)"'

  2. The source is argo-rollouts. Only a deploy that an argo-rollouts DeploySource reported can be acted on, and the Rollout must carry the app's name, in the deploy's namespace. See Deploy sources.

  3. The manager may patch Rollouts. manager.autoAbort.rbacEnabled: true grants patch on rollouts and rollouts/status. Check it:

    kubectl auth can-i patch rollouts.argoproj.io -n <app-ns> --as system:serviceaccount:<ns>:<manager-service-account>
kubectl auth can-i patch rollouts.argoproj.io/status -n <app-ns> --as system:serviceaccount:<ns>:<manager-service-account>

  4. The Rollout waits long enough. It needs a pause step of at least 20 minutes, or the verdict arrives after the release is finished and can only alert.

  5. If you want aborts, grade A must be available. An abort needs grade A evidence, which needs the Postgres log: attribution.arms, the ArmsLog condition True, manager.arms.rbacEnabled for pod logs, and every pod reporting an application_name that starts with its own name. Without it the strongest action is a pause. See Postgres log (grade A).
  6. actuate.namespaces is what you mean. Empty means every namespace. A deploy outside the list is judged and logged and recorded as skipped.
  7. You know the kill switch. kubectl annotate postgreswatch <name> -n <ns> pg-regression-radar.io/actuation-paused=true stops all pausing and aborting at once, with no restart. Remove it to resume. If the watch cannot be read at that moment, the manager assumes it is paused.
  8. You know what a restart forgets. The action ledger (the last 200 attempts) and the breaker's count live in memory. The metrics and the log are the durable record.
  9. Someone reads the alerts. The first real action is a pause, which one click resumes. A pause with nobody watching holds the release.

docs.title: The engine only alerts and does not act
docs.text:
Start with the decision line and its reasons, in the manager log (attribution (...)) and in the verdict at /api/v1/attribution/verdict. Three cases cover almost everything.

  1. "evidence is capped at grade C by: ..." The engine saw a regression but could not prove it was the deploy, so it only alerts. The flags say what held it back:
    • few-donors: fewer than 5 untouched queries with enough history to build a control. A control query needs data for at least half of the 90-minute pre-deploy window, so right after the manager starts or restarts the engine stays at alert for about 45 minutes. Wait, or check that the watch's collector sees enough distinct queries.
    • global-shift: most untouched queries moved the same way at the deploy, so the cause may be load, not the code. The engine cannot separate them without a control arm.
    • table-level: most queries on one table moved together and the deploy did not declare that table.
    • warming-up, transient: the shift is too recent, or was fading, so it is not yet confirmed. Wait for the next evaluation (every 5 minutes).
  2. "seen in 1 of 2 consecutive evaluations required" and "cooldown after the previous action" are guards, not problems: a pause needs the same evidence twice, and a second action waits 10 minutes.

  3. Nothing is paused although the engine wants a hold. The Actuating condition says whether the manager may act at all. If it is True, look at the action ledger (GET /api/v1/attribution/actions) and at the reason of the line after the decision:

    Ledger result Log reason Meaning skipped NamespaceNotAllowed the namespace is not in actuate.namespaces skipped ActuationPaused the kill-switch annotation is set skipped NotArgoRollout the deploy did not come from an argo-rollouts DeploySource failed ActuationFailed the call to the Rollout was refused, usually because manager.autoAbort.rbacEnabled is off, or the Rollout has another name done Acted it acted

  4. The deploy was the first of its app. With no history to compare against the engine says it cannot tell and never convicts it, and there is no earlier revision to roll back to.

The engine cannot convict a deploy before about 15 minutes after it. A Rollout needs a pause step of at least 20 minutes for the action to land in time. See Attribution engine.

docs.title: A line for each step
docs.text: You see The deploy reached Next DeployRegistered only the engine, not yet judged wait for firstEvaluation NoSamples judged and skipped: nothing to read Nothing is detected ShadowMode a decision, not executed the watch is in shadow mode BelowActingThreshold a decision that never acts (none, alert) the first list above VerdictServed a hold or rollback, enforced the rollout controller or actuate acts Acted the Rollout was patched wait for the abort check AbortRecovered / AbortPersisted the abort was checked 15 minutes later persisted twice opens the breaker

docs.title: Grade A needs the Postgres log
docs.text:
A canary and the stable pods can be told apart only by the Postgres log, which records each statement's application_name. The ArmsLog condition says whether that works:

ArmsLog Reason Fix True ArmsUsable nothing False ArmsSettingsRejected a server setting is wrong; the manager log line names the setting, the problem and the fix False ArmsNoLogYet no line has arrived since the manager started; check the log destination and the selector False ArmsLogStale the log stopped flowing for five minutes absent ArmsDisabled is in the log attribution.arms is set and cannot work (no pod-log RBAC, for instance)

When a deploy's pods cannot be told apart you see ArmsUndistinguished and the evidence is B at best. A pause is still possible. See Telling a canary from the stable pods.

docs.title: The circuit breaker
docs.text:
After an abort the engine checks, 15 minutes later, whether the regression went away. If it did not, twice in a row, the breaker opens and the engine only alerts. It is the radar noticing that it is acting on something it cannot fix.

  1. Find out why the aborts did not help: AbortPersisted. The deploy may not have been the cause.

  2. Close the breaker:

    kubectl annotate postgreswatch <name> -n <ns> pg-regression-radar.io/reset-breaker="$(date +%s)" --overwrite

    A new value closes it. A value that was on the object when the manager started does nothing, and the same value twice resets once. Restarting the manager also closes it, and also empties the ledger. 3. Watch for attribution: circuit breaker closed by the reset-breaker annotation (BreakerReset) and for Actuating turning True.

pg_regression_radar_attribution_breaker_open is 1 while it is open: it is a good metric to alert on, because it needs a person.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text: Short answers to the questions that come up after the radar is running.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Each answer is a few lines and points to the page that goes deeper. For a symptom, start at Troubleshooting; for the place to look, at Where to look.

docs.title: Why did the radar wait 10 minutes before judging my deploy?
docs.text: The engine reads the database before and after the deploy and needs enough after to compare. It evaluates from 10 to 45 minutes after, every 5 minutes, and cannot convict before about 15. A Rollout that is promoted in five minutes is out of reach, so give it a pause step of at least 20 minutes. See Enforce mode.

docs.title: What is the difference between shadow and enforce?
docs.text: In shadow the engine judges every deploy and logs what it would do; the verdict endpoint always answers pass (with wouldBe showing the decision) and nothing is changed. In enforce it serves a verdict, and with actuate.enabled the manager pauses or aborts the Rollout itself. Run shadow for a few deploys and compare before you enforce.

docs.title: The watch says Running, so why does it detect nothing?
docs.text: Phase: Running means the worker started. Whether it is reading the database is the Collecting condition, and whether it can act is Actuating. See Nothing is detected.

docs.title: Do I need the Postgres log (attribution.arms)?
docs.text: Only to abort. Through pg_stat_statements alone the best evidence is grade B and the strongest action a pause, which a person can resume with one click. An abort needs grade A, which needs the Postgres log to tell the canary from the stable pods. See Grade A needs the Postgres log.

docs.title: Is it a problem that the Actuating condition is False?
docs.text: It is a status, not an error, and the reason says why: in shadow mode it is ShadowMode, and without attribution.actuate it is ActuationNotAsked. It is a problem only if you expected the manager to act. See Enforce mode.

docs.title: How do I turn the engine off quickly?
docs.text: Annotate the watch: kubectl annotate postgreswatch <name> -n <ns> pg-regression-radar.io/actuation-paused=true. Nothing is paused or aborted until you remove it, and no restart is needed. The engine keeps judging and logging.

docs.title: What happens when the manager restarts?
docs.text: The collector's samples, the action ledger (the last 200 attempts) and the circuit breaker's count are in memory and start empty. A deploy that had not been judged yet cannot be: it logs NoSamples. The metrics and the log are the durable record; the dashboard's history is kept in memory too unless --observe-history=postgres.

docs.title: Why is only one manager pod doing anything?
docs.text: Leader election: with more than one replica exactly one runs the watches and serves the webhook, the metrics and the verdict listeners; a standby takes over if the leader goes. Find the leader in the Lease pg-regression-radar-manager.radar.pgregressionradar.io. A request that a Service sends to a standby is refused: see A Service can send an event to a standby.

docs.title: Are the logs JSON?
docs.text: Yes, on every command, and since 1.9.2 on every line. Earlier releases of the manager mixed JSON, controller-runtime's own format and plain text. Use --log-format=text for a terminal. See Logs.

docs.title: How do I get more detail?
docs.text: --log-level=debug (chart: manager.logLevel: debug). It writes a line per query per scrape, so turn it on for one investigation. --zap-log-level still works and is mapped.

docs.title: A log message changed between releases. Is that a break?
docs.text: No. Messages are sentences and can be reworded; the reason field is the stable part, and each code has an entry in Reason codes. Match on reason in alerts and parsers.

docs.title: Where did the old Troubleshooting page go?
docs.text: It is now a section of its own. The database-side errors are in Setup and the database, "nothing is detected" in its own page, and the attribution engine in Enforce mode.

docs.title: Log catalog
docs.text: Every message the radar writes, with its level, the fields it carries, and what it means.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This page lists each log message by the part of the radar that writes it. Find a message you saw with your browser's search, read what it means, and follow the link when it has a reason code. A message is free text and can be reworded between releases; the reason code is the part that stays. How to read the log and how to turn on more detail is on the Logs page.

A test compares this page with the source on every build: a message that is logged and is not here, or listed here and not logged, or a field that does not match, fails it. A message that ends in … is built at run time and the text after it varies.

Fields that controller-runtime adds to every line written while it reconciles an object (controller, controllerKind, name, namespace, reconcileID) are described on Logs, and are not repeated in the rows.

docs.title: Manager: start-up and shutdown
docs.text:
What manager writes while it starts. Almost every error here ends the process, and the pod restarts.

Level Message Fields What it means and what to do info http server listening server addr One of the manager's HTTP servers is up. server names it (webhook, pg-metrics, dashboard-api, attribution-verdict, observe) and addr is where it listens. Every manager pod serves dashboard-api; the others start only on the leader, so a follower does not log them. error invalid --alerting-allowed-destinations err The allowlist could not be parsed. The manager exits. Use comma-separated hostnames, IPs or CIDRs. error invalid --cluster-health-check-interval value: must be positive value The interval must be positive. The manager exits. error invalid --security-profile value value allowed --security-profile is not controlled or hardened. The manager exits; allowed lists the choices. error invalid alerting destination policy configuration err The policy and the allowlist or relay URL do not fit (for example allowlist with no list, or relay-only with no URL). The manager exits. error invalid logging flag err --log-level or --log-format has a value that is not accepted. The process exits with a non-zero code. Use debug, info, warn or error, and json or text. error invalid or unreachable observe history err --observe-history is postgres and the store could not be opened with the DSN in --observe-history-dsn-file. The manager exits. Fix the DSN, or use memory. warn logging: … A deprecated --zap-* flag was passed and was mapped to --log-level or --log-format (or ignored). Replace it with the new flag; the line says which. error problem running manager err The manager stopped with an error after it had started. The pod restarts. Read err. info starting manager leaderElection Everything is registered and the manager is starting. leaderElection says whether it will wait for the lease. After it, the leader logs postgreswatch worker started for each watch. error unable to add attribution verdict server err The verdict endpoint could not be added (--attribution-verdict-addr). The manager exits. error unable to add dashboard API server err The read-only dashboard API could not be added (--dashboard-addr). The manager exits. error unable to add observe history recorder err The recorder that writes the dashboard's history could not be added. The manager exits. error unable to add observe server err The Observe API the live dashboard reads (--observe-addr) could not be added. The manager exits. error unable to add pg-metrics server err The Postgres query metrics listener could not be added (--pg-metrics-bind-address). The manager exits. error unable to add webhook server err The deploy-event webhook listener could not be added (--webhook-bind-address). The manager exits; check for an address already in use. error unable to build Kubernetes client; attribution.arms.podLogs will have no effect err The client used to read Postgres pod logs could not be built, so attribution.arms.podLogs does nothing (reason ArmsDisabled). error unable to build direct Kubernetes client for startup failure reporting err The manager could not build the client it uses to write a startup failure into the status of its custom resources. A startup failure will still be logged, but not shown in kubectl get postgreswatch. error unable to build dynamic client; PostgresWatch.spec.autoAbort will have no effect err The client used to patch Rollouts could not be built, so spec.autoAbort does nothing. Fix the in-cluster configuration. error unable to create controller err controller A controller could not be registered. The manager exits. controller says which (PostgresWatch, DeploySource, WorkloadWatch, PostgresRadarCluster); the usual cause is a missing CRD, so check kubectl get crd | grep radar. error unable to report manager startup failure in custom resource status err The manager failed to start and then also failed to write the failure into the custom resources' status. Read the line before this one: that is the real failure. error unable to resolve Kubernetes API server config err The manager found neither an in-cluster configuration nor a kubeconfig. Outside a cluster, set KUBECONFIG; inside one, check that the pod has its service account token. error unable to set up health check err The /healthz endpoint could not be registered. The manager exits. error unable to set up ready check err The /readyz endpoint could not be registered. The manager exits. error unable to start manager err controller-runtime could not start (the API server is unreachable, or the cache could not sync). The manager exits and the pod restarts. Read err.

docs.title: PostgresWatch, DeploySource and workloads
docs.text:
The controllers. They run on the leader only.

Level Message Fields What it means and what to do warn attribution: circuit breaker closed by the reset-breaker annotation, the engine may act again reason watch token An operator closed the circuit breaker: BreakerReset. info attribution: reset-breaker annotation changed, but the circuit breaker was already closed watch token Someone set pg-regression-radar.io/reset-breaker while the breaker was closed. Nothing changed. info deploysource deleted, webhook route removed The DeploySource was deleted and its webhook route removed. Events sent to that path now get 404. info deploysource has an invalid spec, route not registered reason err The DeploySource's spec was rejected and no route is registered: InvalidSpec. info deploysource watched natively, no webhook route registered reason sourceType appName A kubernetes or argo-rollouts source is watched through the API, so it has no webhook route: NativeWatchActive. info deploysource webhook route registered reason path sourceType The webhook route is live at path: RouteRegistered. warn ignoring unknown spec.multipleTesting reason watch value err The value is not one the radar knows, and was ignored: MultipleTestingUnknown. error list postgresradarclusters for secret-triggered health check err The manager could not list PostgresRadarClusters after a kubeconfig Secret changed, so the immediate re-check was skipped. The next scheduled check still runs. Usually a transient API error. warn postgresradarcluster health check failed reason cluster err A remote cluster's kubeconfig does not work: ClusterHealthCheckFailed. info postgreswatch deleted, worker stopped The PostgresWatch was deleted and its collector and engine were stopped. Its in-memory samples and action ledger went with it. info postgreswatch worker started reason cluster The watch's collector and engine are running: WorkerStarted. It is logged again whenever the spec changes, because the worker is replaced. error postgreswatch: alert notify failed reason watch regression err An alert for a regression tied to a deploy was not delivered: AlertNotifyFailed. error postgreswatch: attribution revert disabled by invalid configuration reason watch err Draft revert pull requests are off because attribution.revert is wrong: RevertDisabled. The engine keeps working. info postgreswatch: attribution.actuate ignored, it only acts in enforce mode reason watch attribution.actuate is set but the watch is in shadow mode, so nothing will be paused or aborted: ShadowMode. info postgreswatch: attribution.actuate ignored, no Argo Rollouts actuator is available (enable manager.autoAbort.rbacEnabled) reason watch attribution.actuate is set but the manager has no Argo Rollouts RBAC: NoActuator. error postgreswatch: auto-abort failed reason watch rollout confidence err The p-value auto-abort tried to abort a Rollout and failed: AutoAbortFailed. info postgreswatch: auto-abort skipped, deploysource not found reason watch source err The p-value auto-abort found a regression and no DeploySource to act through: AutoAbortSkipped. Normal for sources that have no abort action. info postgreswatch: auto-abort triggered reason watch rollout confidence query The p-value auto-abort aborted a Rollout: AutoAbortTriggered. error postgreswatch: collector exited unexpectedly reason watch err The collector stopped on its own: CollectorExited. The watch stops scraping until its worker is replaced. error postgreswatch: failed to persist PerformanceRegression CR reason watch regression err The regression was detected and alerted but could not be saved as a PerformanceRegression: RegressionPersistFailed. error postgreswatch: failed to persist periodic PerformanceRegression CR reason watch regression err A periodic regression could not be saved as a PerformanceRegression: RegressionPersistFailed. error postgreswatch: periodic alert notify failed reason watch regression err An alert for a periodic regression (not tied to a deploy) was not delivered: AlertNotifyFailed. info postgreswatch: spec.autoAbort ignored, attribution.actuate decides instead reason watch The older p-value auto-abort stands down because attribution.actuate decides: AutoAbortIgnored. info remoteClusterSecretRef is deprecated; register the cluster as a PostgresRadarCluster and use remoteClusterRef instead watch namespace see The watch uses the deprecated remoteClusterSecretRef. It still works. Register the cluster as a PostgresRadarCluster and use remoteClusterRef; see points to the page. error unable to resolve DSN err reason The watch's connection string could not be read from its Secret: DSNUnresolved. error unable to resolve referenced secrets err reason A Secret the watch refers to besides the DSN could not be read: SecretsUnresolved. error unable to start watch worker err reason The watch's worker could not be built: WorkerStartFailed. The watch shows Phase: Failed. info workloadwatch: deploy event synthesised from native rollout reason kind workload revision deploySource A Rollout or Deployment finished a new revision and the manager made a deploy event from it: DeployEventSynthesised. info workloadwatch: postgresWatchRef not ready yet, will retry reason deploySource workload kind A deploy was seen but its PostgresWatch is not running yet, so it will be retried rather than lost: PostgresWatchNotReady.

docs.title: Attribution engine
docs.text:
Judging deploys, acting on Rollouts and reading the Postgres log. These lines carry a reason code.

Level Message Fields What it means and what to do info attribution (enforce): decision below the acting threshold, nothing to execute Enforce mode, and the decision is none or alert: BelowActingThreshold. info attribution (enforce): verdict served to the rollout controller A hold or rollback decision, enforced and now served at the verdict endpoint: VerdictServed. info attribution (shadow): decision, not executed The engine judged a deploy and the watch is in shadow mode, so nothing was done: ShadowMode. action is what it would have done; reasons says why. info attribution (shadow): would open a draft revert pull request, not opened deploy revision grade Shadow mode, and a deploy was convicted at hold or above: this is the pull request the radar would open in enforce mode. Nothing was sent to GitHub. warn attribution.arms: cannot read the server's settings reason watch err The Postgres settings could not be read, retried every 30 seconds: ArmsSettingsUnread. info attribution.arms: the Postgres log can serve as an arm-labelled source reason watch sampleRate The log is usable: ArmsUsable. warn attribution.arms: the Postgres log cannot be used yet One Postgres setting stops the log from being used: ArmsSettingsRejected. setting, value, problem and fix name it and say what to set. warn attribution.arms: the Postgres log setting costs more than it needs to The log works, but a setting makes it cost more than it needs to. setting, problem and fix say which; this line has no reason code because nothing is wrong. info attribution: acted on the rollout reason deploy rollout action grade impact reasons The Rollout was paused or aborted: Acted. warn attribution: actuation paused by annotation, nothing paused or aborted reason deploy action The engine wanted to act but the kill switch is on: ActuationPaused. warn attribution: cannot tell the arms of a deploy apart reason deploy err The pods of the canary and the stable arm could not be told apart for this evaluation, which falls back to grade B at best: ArmsUndistinguished. info attribution: checked the abort reason deploy result detail The check after an abort: result is recovered (AbortRecovered) or persisted (AbortPersisted). warn attribution: circuit breaker open, the engine will only alert until it is reset reason deploy result detail howToReset Two aborts in a row did not help and the engine now only alerts: BreakerOpen. howToReset says how to close it. error attribution: could not act on the rollout, will retry at the next evaluation reason deploy rollout action err The pause or abort call failed: ActuationFailed. It is retried at the next evaluation. info attribution: could not check the abort, too little data after it reason deploy The check 15 minutes after an abort had too little data: AbortUnverifiable. info attribution: deploy registered, it will be judged from 10 to 45 minutes after it reason deploy namespace app revision source firstEvaluation lastEvaluation The engine tracks this deploy: DeployRegistered. firstEvaluation and lastEvaluation bound when it is judged. info attribution: draft revert pull request deploy outcome detail url The result of an attempt to open a draft revert pull request. outcome is opened, already-proposed, skipped (a guard declined) or failed, and detail explains it. info attribution: namespace not allowed for actuation, nothing paused or aborted reason deploy namespace action The engine wanted to act but the namespace is not allowed: NamespaceNotAllowed. warn attribution: no query samples to judge the deploy by, evaluation skipped reason deploy namespace app An evaluation was skipped because there is nothing to read: NoSamples. info attribution: not an Argo Rollouts deploy, nothing to pause or abort reason deploy source action The engine wanted to act but the deploy is not a Rollout from an argo-rollouts source: NotArgoRollout. error postgreswatch: attribution.arms disabled, … reason watch attribution.arms is configured but cannot work, so grade A evidence is off: ArmsDisabled. The text after the comma says why.

docs.title: Dashboard history
docs.text:
The record behind the live dashboard.

Level Message Fields What it means and what to do warn observe history: cannot record; the radar keeps acting, history will have a gap reason err The dashboard's history store could not be written: HistoryNotRecording. Decisions are not affected. debug observe history: series not stored deploy err Debug. A deploy's query series could not be saved to the history. Only seen with --log-level=debug.

docs.title: Collector
docs.text:
Reading pg_stat_statements. The standalone collector command writes the same lines.

Level Message Fields What it means and what to do error collector exited with error err The collector stopped with an error and the process exits. Read err. info collector: detected PostgreSQL older than 13; using legacy pg_stat_statements column names (total_time/mean_time) server_version_num The server is older than 13, so the collector reads the legacy column names (total_time, mean_time). Informational. info collector: metrics server listening addr The standalone collector's metrics endpoint is up on addr. info collector: pg_stat_statements counters restarted for query; using activity since the reset query_id calls stats_since A query's counters went backwards: a pg_stat_statements_reset(), an eviction or a crash. The collector uses only the activity since the reset. If this is frequent for many queries, something is resetting the statistics. debug collector: plan capture failed for query, skipping query_id err Debug. A plan could not be captured for one query and was skipped. info collector: plan-diff capture unavailable (requires PostgreSQL 16+ for EXPLAIN GENERIC_PLAN); continuing without it err spec.capturePlans is on and the server cannot run EXPLAIN (GENERIC_PLAN), which needs PostgreSQL 16 or newer. Detection continues without plan diffs. error collector: scrape failed err One scrape of pg_stat_statements failed. Read err: relation "pg_stat_statements" does not exist and permission denied are covered in Setup. The next scrape tries again; the Collecting condition turns False after three missed intervals. info collector: starting scrape loop interval retention cluster The collector started. interval is the scrape interval and retention how long samples stay in memory. info collector: stopping The collector's context was cancelled: the watch was deleted or its spec changed, or the process is shutting down. error --dry-run: collector ping failed err --dry-run could not reach the database. Read err, and see Setup. info --dry-run: configuration and connectivity OK version --dry-run connected to the database and exits with code 0. error --dsn is required No --dsn was given. The process exits with code 1. error failed to create collector err The collector could not be built from the flags, usually a malformed --dsn. The process exits. error --max-query-text-len must be positive value The flag must be above zero. The process exits. error metrics server error err The metrics server stopped with an error, usually because the address is in use (--listen). error metrics server shutdown error err The metrics server did not shut down cleanly. Informational.

docs.title: Correlation engine
docs.text:
Detecting regressions. Lines marked debug only appear with --log-level=debug.

Level Message Fields What it means and what to do info correlation: analysing deploy event_id query_count window_minutes The correlation engine started comparing the queries before and after a deploy. query_count is how many it looks at. debug correlation: change point too far from deploy, rejecting query_id change_at deploy_at distance tolerance Debug. A change was found, but too far from the deploy time to be blamed on it. info correlation: deploy event registered for retry event_id deploy_at retry_until A deploy arrived before the radar had enough history. It is retried until retry_until. info correlation: deploy event's analysis window elapsed event_id queries_detected The retry window ended. queries_detected is how many regressions were found for the deploy in total. debug correlation: detection did not survive multiple-testing control query_id p_value mode queries_tested Debug. A detection was dropped by the multiple-testing control (mode) because many queries were tested at once. debug correlation: insufficient data, not yet ready to evaluate query_id pre_samples post_samples min_samples pre_executions post_executions min_executions executions_checked Debug. A query does not have enough samples or executions yet before and after the deploy; the engine waits and tries again. info correlation: multiple-testing control removed detections mode queries_tested detected_before removed level The multiple-testing control removed removed of detected_before detections. Informational; set spec.multipleTesting: none to turn it off. debug correlation: no change point found, rejecting naive mean shift query_id change_factor Debug. The mean shifted but no change point was found in the series, so the naive shift was rejected as noise. info correlation: periodic analysis query_count window_minutes now The scheduled analysis, which looks for regressions not tied to a deploy, ran over the retained window. info correlation: periodic regression detected query_id change_factor confidence change_at A query regressed with no deploy to blame, and passed every test. info correlation: periodic regression newly detected, suppressing until recovery query_id confidence A periodic regression was reported once and is now suppressed until the query recovers, so it does not alert again. info correlation: periodic regression recovered, re-arming query_id status A suppressed periodic regression recovered and is armed again. info correlation: regression detected query_id change_factor confidence change_at A query regressed after a deploy and passed every test. A PerformanceRegression and an alert follow. change_factor is the new latency over the old. debug correlation: t-test result query_id p_value change_factor change_at Debug. The significance test of one query: p_value, change_factor and the change_at it found.

docs.title: Deploy events
docs.text:
Receiving deploy events. The standalone ingester command writes the same lines.

Level Message Fields What it means and what to do info --dry-run: configuration OK version listen apiServerHost --dry-run found the configuration valid and exits with code 0. error --dry-run: invalid --listen address value err --listen is not a valid address. Exits. error --dry-run: unknown --source-type value --source-type is not one the ingester knows. Exits. error events handler: encode err The response for /events could not be encoded. Informational. warn ingester: OTLP spans matched but were rejected rejected detail Spans matched the mapping and were rejected. detail says why (for example a missing app name or revision attribute). debug ingester: deploy event ignored, its app is not the one this source is configured for id app configuredApp Debug. The event is for an app other than the DeploySource's appName, so it was dropped and the sender still got 204. If you expected this deploy to be judged, app and configuredApp show the mismatch. warn ingester: deploy event not stored, the watch this source feeds is not running source A webhook arrived for a DeploySource whose PostgresWatch is not running, so the event was not stored. The sender gets 503 with Retry-After: 10 and can send it again; start the watch (see PostgresWatchNotReady). info ingester: deploy event stored id app revision timestamp A deploy event was received and stored for the watch. It is followed by attribution: deploy registered. If you do not see this line for a deploy, the event never arrived: see A deploy never shows up. error ingester: failed to decode OTLP request err The OTLP request body could not be decoded. Check the exporter's protocol and content type. error ingester: failed to parse webhook source_type err The body is not the format source_type expects. Check the sender's payload against Deploy sources. info ingester: listening addr source_type The standalone ingester is up on addr. error ingester: otlp source is misconfigured err An otlp source has no usable span mapping, so every request is answered with 500. err says what is wrong with the mapping; fix it in the DeploySource or the ingester flags. warn ingester: rejected /events request with invalid or missing token remote_addr A read of /events had an invalid or missing token and was refused. warn ingester: rejected webhook request with invalid or missing token source_type remote_addr A webhook arrived with an invalid or missing token and was refused with 401. Send X-Webhook-Token, or check remote_addr if you do not recognise the sender. error invalid OTLP flags err The OTLP flags do not fit the --source-type. The process exits. error invalid deploy source configuration err The deploy source configuration is unusable (an otlp source without a mapping). The process exits. error server error err The ingester's HTTP server stopped with an error, usually an address already in use.

docs.title: Alerting, OTLP export, Prometheus and storage
docs.text:
Everything that leaves the radar or is stored by it.

Level Message Fields What it means and what to do info alerting: notification sent regression status_code An alert was delivered. status_code is the destination's answer. info alerting: notification skipped; webhook url is not configured regression A regression was detected but the watch has no alert URL, so nothing was sent. warn otlpexport: delivery failed, will retry attempt in err One delivery attempt failed. It is retried after in. error otlpexport: giving up on regression regression endpoint err Delivery failed after every retry and the regression was not exported. err is the last failure. warn otlpexport: queue full, dropping regression regression endpoint Regressions are produced faster than the OTLP exporter delivers them, and one was dropped. Check the collector endpoint's health. warn promsource: query failed; the engine will see no samples until this is fixed operation err A query against Prometheus failed. Until it is fixed the engine sees no samples, which shows up as NoSamples: NoSamples. operation is samples_in_range or all_query_ids. error storage: prune failed store err A prune sweep failed. Read err; it is retried at the next interval. info storage: prune loop started store interval retention The state store's prune loop started. debug storage: prune swept store cutoff Debug. A prune sweep finished; rows older than cutoff were removed. warn storage: retention <= 0, disabling prune loop store The retention is zero or negative, so the prune loop is off and the state store grows without bound.

docs.text:
What the operator command writes. It shares the collector, correlation and ingester lines above.

Level Message Fields What it means and what to do error dashboard API server error err The dashboard API stopped with an error. error --dry-run: --periodic-interval-minutes must be positive value The interval must be positive. Exits. error --dry-run: --periodic-window-minutes must be positive value The window must be positive. Exits. error --dry-run: invalid alerting configuration err --dry-run found invalid alerting settings. Exits. error --dry-run: postgres state backend connection failed err --dry-run could not reach the state backend. Exits. error --dry-run: unknown --state-backend (want memory or postgres) value --state-backend is not memory or postgres. Exits. error failed to configure OTLP export err The OTLP exporter could not be built. Exits. error failed to configure alerting err The alerting flags are invalid. Exits. error failed to initialise postgres state backend err --state-backend=postgres could not connect or create its schema. Exits. error failed to read --alert-template-file err The alert template file could not be read. Exits. error invalid --dsn err The connection string is malformed. The process exits. error invalid --multiple-testing err --multiple-testing is not an allowed value. Exits. error invalid --state-dsn err The state backend's DSN is malformed. Exits. error invalid OTLP export configuration err The OTLP export flags are invalid. Exits. warn operator: backfill: list query ids failed, starting with cold sample history err On start the operator could not read the stored query ids, so it starts with an empty sample history. warn operator: backfill: load events failed, starting with cold event history err The stored deploy events could not be read, so it starts with no event history. warn operator: backfill: load samples failed query_id err The stored samples of one query could not be loaded; that query starts cold. info operator: backfilled collector sample history samples query_ids Stored samples were loaded back after a restart. info operator: backfilled event history events cursor Stored deploy events were loaded back after a restart. info operator: dashboard API server listening addr The dashboard API is up on addr. info operator: exporting regressions as OTLP logs url OTLP export is on and sends to url. info operator: metrics server listening addr The metrics listener is up on addr. error operator: notify failed err regression An alert was not delivered (the operator's counterpart of AlertNotifyFailed). error operator: periodic notify failed err regression A periodic alert was not delivered (the operator's counterpart of AlertNotifyFailed). error operator: persist event failed err event_id A deploy event could not be written to the state backend. error operator: persist sample failed err query_id A sample could not be written to the state backend. The radar keeps running from memory; history will have a gap after a restart. info operator: postgres state backend enabled schema retention prune_interval separate_state_dsn Samples and events are persisted to Postgres and survive a restart. separate_state_dsn is whether it is a different database from the monitored one. info operator: webhook server listening addr The webhook listener is up on addr. info security profile security-profile The operator started with this --security-profile. error unknown --state-backend (want memory or postgres) value --state-backend is not memory or postgres. Exits. error webhook server error err The webhook listener stopped with an error, usually an address in use.

The read-only API and the pg-regression-radar dashboard command.

Level Message Fields What it means and what to do warn dashboard: cannot reach the manager err pg-regression-radar dashboard lost its port-forward to the manager. It retries. Check that the manager pod runs and that you may get pods and port-forward. info dashboard: connected to the manager pod The dashboard is connected to the manager pod pod. info dashboard: the leader changed from to The leader moved from one manager pod to another and the dashboard followed it. error dashboardapi: list deploys failed err The dashboard API could not read deploys from its store. The request gets 500. error dashboardapi: list query ids failed err The dashboard API could not list query ids. docs.title: Logs
docs.text: One format for every line, how to read it, how to ask for more detail, and recipes to find what you need.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Every command the radar ships (manager, operator, collector, ingester) writes its log to standard output, one JSON object per line, through one handler. The radar's own code, controller-runtime and anything that logs before the flags are read all come out the same way, so one jq filter works on the whole stream. Since 1.9.2 there is also one switch for the level and one for the format.

{"time":"2026-11-27T15:04:05.000-03:00","level":"INFO","msg":"attribution: acted on the rollout","reason":"Acted","deploy":"d1","rollout":"checkout","action":"abort","grade":"A","impact":0.12}

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Flag Values Default Effect --log-level debug, info, warn, error info The least severe line that is written. debug adds the evaluation and scrape details that are normally left out. --log-format json, text json json is one object per line. text is key=value, easier to read in a terminal.

With Helm, set manager.logLevel and manager.logFormat (both empty by default, which means info and json). In the lab, add the flags to the args of the pgrr-manager container.

The old --zap-* flags still work

The manager used to take controller-runtime's --zap-log-level, --zap-encoder and --zap-devel. They are accepted and mapped (--zap-log-level=debug to --log-level=debug, --zap-encoder=console to --log-format=text, --zap-devel to both), and the manager logs one logging: line saying what it did. An explicit --log-level or --log-format wins over them. Any other --zap-* flag is accepted and has no effect. Replace them when you next edit the Deployment.

A value that is not accepted stops the process with a message naming the allowed values.

docs.title: Format
docs.text: Field Meaning time When the line was written, RFC 3339. level DEBUG, INFO, WARN or ERROR. msg What happened, as a sentence. It can be reworded between releases; match on reason instead when there is one. reason A stable reason code, on lines that explain a decision or a fault. err The error text, on a line about a failure.

docs.title: Fields you can rely on
docs.text:
The names below are the same on every line that has them.

Field Where Meaning watch watch and arms lines the PostgresWatch, as namespace/name deploy attribution lines the deploy event id app, namespace, revision deploy lines what was deployed, and where action attribution lines none, alert, hold or rollback for a decision, pause or abort for something done grade attribution lines the evidence grade, A to D detail lines that carry a reason one sentence about this occurrence. Free text goes here, never in reason. source, source_type deploy event lines the DeploySource, and its type

Lines written by controller-runtime itself (the manager's own start-up, "Starting workers", "Reconciler error") carry the fields it adds while it reconciles an object:

{"level":"ERROR","msg":"Reconciler error","controller":"postgreswatch","controllerGroup":"radar.pgregressionradar.io","controllerKind":"PostgresWatch","PostgresWatch":{"name":"w","namespace":"ns"},"namespace":"ns","name":"w","reconcileID":"abc","logger":"controller-runtime","err":"..."}

controller, controllerKind and reconcileID say which reconciler and which pass; namespace and name the object; logger which controller-runtime component. They are not repeated in the log catalog.

docs.title: Levels
docs.text:
Level What it is for Example error Something the radar was asked to do did not happen. attribution: could not act on the rollout, will retry at the next evaluation warn It keeps working, and an operator may want to look. attribution: no query samples to judge the deploy by, evaluation skipped info A normal event or a deliberate choice, especially every decision the engine makes. attribution: deploy registered, ... debug Per-scrape and per-query detail. Off by default because there is a line for each query. correlation: t-test result

Turn debug on for one investigation and back off after, because it writes a line per query per scrape.

docs.title: Recipes
docs.text:
Every recipe reads the manager log. Put one of these in front:

LOG='kubectl logs -n <ns> -l app.kubernetes.io/component=manager --since=2h --tail=-1'

What went wrong lately

$LOG | jq -c 'select(.level == "ERROR" or .level == "WARN") | {time, level, msg, reason, err}'

Everything about one deploy

$LOG | jq -c 'select(.deploy == "<deploy id>")'

Every decision the engine made, and why

$LOG | jq -r 'select(.msg | startswith("attribution")) | select(.action) | "\(.time) \(.deploy) \(.action) grade=\(.grade) \(.reason)"'

Which reasons are being emitted, and how often

$LOG | jq -r 'select(.reason) | .reason' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn

One watch

$LOG | jq -c 'select(.watch == "<ns>/<name>")'

The same, from a log shipper. The fields above are plain top-level keys, so a Loki query {app="pg-regression-radar-manager"} | json | reason="BreakerOpen" or an Elasticsearch filter on reason works without parsing.

A crash loop. The line before the restart is in the previous container:

kubectl logs -n <ns> deploy/<manager> --previous | tail -20

docs.title: Alerting on logs
docs.text: Alert on the reason, not on the message. A reason is a code that stays; a message is a sentence that gets reworded. The reasons worth an alert are marked warn or error in the reason codes; BreakerOpen, ArmsSettingsRejected, ArmsLogStale and ActuationFailed are a good start. The same conditions exist as metrics and as status conditions.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text: Every Prometheus metric the radar exports, with its type, its labels and what a value tells you.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Metrics answer "how much, and since when", where a log line answers "what happened". They are the signal to alert on, and the one to graph over days. A test compares this page with the source on every build, so a metric that is exported and not listed here, or listed and not exported, or whose type or labels differ, fails it.

All names start with pg_regression_radar_. Most carry a constant cluster label with the name of the watched cluster, which is not repeated in the rows. The Labels column lists the labels that vary.

docs.title: Where to read them
docs.text:
• Postgres and attribution metrics. The manager serves them per watch on --pg-metrics-bind-address (default :9090), at /metrics. Only the leader serves them.
  • Controller-runtime metrics (reconcile counts and durations, work queue depth, client request rates) are served on --metrics-bind-address, which is 0 (off) by default. They are not listed here because they are not the radar's.
  • Standalone collector and all-in-one operator. --listen on the collector command, and the operator's metrics address, serve the collector metrics.
kubectl -n <ns> port-forward deploy/<manager> 9090:9090
curl -s localhost:9090/metrics | grep '^pg_regression_radar_'

docs.title: Collector
docs.text: Metric Type Labels What it tells you pg_regression_radar_collector_scrapes_total counter Scrapes of pg_stat_statements performed. It should rise once per scrape interval; flat means the collector is not scraping (see ScrapeStale). pg_regression_radar_collector_scrape_errors_total counter Scrapes that failed. Compare its rate with the scrapes counter; a rising rate means the log has collector: scrape failed lines. pg_regression_radar_collector_tracked_queries gauge Distinct query ids held in memory. Zero after the first scrapes means nothing is being collected. pg_regression_radar_collector_retained_samples_total gauge Samples currently held in memory across all queries. It grows until retention is reached, then stays flat. pg_regression_radar_collector_stats_resets_detected_total counter Times a query's counters went backwards (a reset, an eviction or a crash). Frequent resets mean something is calling pg_stat_statements_reset() or evicting entries. pg_regression_radar_collector_explain_statements_skipped_total counter Rows skipped because their text is itself an EXPLAIN. A sustained rate points at something other than the radar issuing raw EXPLAINs against the database. pg_regression_radar_query_mean_exec_time_ms gauge queryid Mean execution time of a query over its whole lifetime in pg_stat_statements, at the last scrape. pg_regression_radar_query_interval_mean_exec_time_ms gauge queryid Mean execution time of the calls made since the previous scrape. This is the series the radar judges; it is absent when the interval is unknown or had no calls. pg_regression_radar_query_calls_total gauge queryid Cumulative calls from pg_stat_statements. It is a gauge because it is copied from Postgres, and goes down after a reset.

docs.title: Attribution engine
docs.text: Metric Type Labels What it tells you pg_regression_radar_attribution_shadow_decisions_total counter action grade Decisions the engine reached in shadow mode, which were never executed. action is what it would have done. pg_regression_radar_attribution_actions_total counter action result Pauses and aborts of Argo Rollouts, by action (pause, abort) and result (done, failed, skipped). skipped is a decision the engine did not carry out (namespace not allowed, kill switch, not a Rollout); failed matches an ActuationFailed log line. pg_regression_radar_attribution_verifications_total counter result Checks made after an abort: recovered or persisted. Persisted ones count toward the circuit breaker. pg_regression_radar_attribution_breaker_open gauge 1 while the circuit breaker is open and the engine only alerts (BreakerOpen). A good alert: it needs a person. pg_regression_radar_attribution_revert_proposals_total counter result Draft revert pull requests, by result: opened, already-proposed, skipped (a guard declined) or failed (the GitHub call failed).

docs.title: Arms: the Postgres log behind grade A
docs.text: Metric Type Labels What it tells you pg_regression_radar_attribution_arms_usable gauge 1 when the Postgres log is flowing and its settings allow grade A evidence. 0 is the same condition as ArmsLog being False; see ArmsSettingsRejected, ArmsNoLogYet and ArmsLogStale. pg_regression_radar_attribution_arms_records_total counter Statement executions read from the Postgres log. Flat while arms_usable is 1 means the workload is idle. pg_regression_radar_attribution_arms_dropped_total counter Executions dropped because the log had too many distinct application_name and query pairs. Rising means arm evidence is being thinned.

docs.title: Detection and alerting
docs.text: Metric Type Labels What it tells you pg_regression_radar_regressions_detected_total counter trigger cluster Regressions that passed every test, by trigger (deploy or periodic) and the watched cluster. pg_regression_radar_pending_deploy_events gauge Deploy events still being retried until their analysis window closes. A value that stays high means deploys keep arriving before the radar has enough history. pg_regression_radar_periodic_regressions_in_progress gauge Queries currently suppressed under an already-reported periodic regression. pg_regression_radar_notifications_total counter status format Alert delivery attempts, by final status (success or error) and payload format. A rising error count matches AlertNotifyFailed.

docs.title: Exporters and sources
docs.text: Metric Type Labels What it tells you pg_regression_radar_otlp_export_total counter result Regressions handed to the OTLP log exporter, by result (success, failed, dropped). pg_regression_radar_promsource_query_errors_total counter operation Failed queries against the Prometheus sample source, by operation (samples_in_range, all_query_ids). Any rise means the engine may see no samples (NoSamples).

docs.title: Useful alerts
docs.text:
- alert: PgrrBreakerOpen
  expr: pg_regression_radar_attribution_breaker_open == 1
  for: 5m
- alert: PgrrNotScraping
  expr: rate(pg_regression_radar_collector_scrapes_total[10m]) == 0
  for: 10m
- alert: PgrrArmsUnusable
  expr: pg_regression_radar_attribution_arms_usable == 0
  for: 15m
- alert: PgrrAlertsNotDelivered
  expr: increase(pg_regression_radar_notifications_total{status="error"}[1h]) > 0
